newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals slip, more losses seen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals slip, more losses seen.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures ended lower on Monday on continued bearishness after gold fell to a four-and-a-quarter-year low of $334.00 an ounce in New York on Friday, traders said.
Activity was dull due to a market holiday in Hong Kong.
Gold prices ranged from flat to 16 yen per gram lower.
Benchmark June closed 12 yen easier at 1,221 yen.

"Large-lot bargain-hunting buying is unlikely to emerge unless benchmark June gold falls below 1,200 yen," one trader said. Spot gold was quoted at $334.50/345.00 per ounce at 0727 GMT, against $334.30/80 in New York on Friday.
Focus in the gold market was on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on Tuesday and Wednesday this week.
Widespread views that the FOMC will leave interest rates unchanged have led to strength in U.S. stocks and have put downward pressure on gold prices, the traders said.

In platinum group metals (PGM) futures, private investors were tending to build fresh short positions amid growing expectations that term shipments of Russian PGMs will arrive in Japan later this week. Traders said, however, that the resumption of Russian sales would not immediately resolve tightness in the physical market.

"If Russia resumes only contracted sales (no spot sales) to Japanese customers, the tightness in palladium supplies will not change," one trader said. "High PGM lease rates are likely to persist for some time," he said.
A large overhang in TOCOM short positions was seen contributing to the high lease rates, they said.
Palladium futures ranged from flat to 14 yen per gram weaker. Benchmark June palladium was off nine yen at 487 yen.
Benchmark June platinum finished down nine yen at 1,351 yen. Benchmark June silver was off 1.9 yen per 10 grams at 174.8 yen. --Tokyo Commodities Desk, +81-3-3432-7431
